App itakuwa na jumla ya hizo template,ambazo ndani yao/ndani ya kila template kutakuwa na MASOMO 12 yenye uzito mkubwa.
App inaitwa Giniaz College.

**Defining Project Scope**

Okay, I'm setting the groundwork. My focus is on conceptualizing a React-based educational platform, dubbed "Giniaz College." The primary goal is to provide a platform with various courses. I am starting to flesh out the foundational requirements, starting with the app's name: Giniaz.


**Developing Core Features**

Right now, I'm concentrating on the functional aspects. I've got the app name, "Giniaz College," down. The goal is to build an educational platform and I'm organizing the content around the course templates. I'm thinking of building course categories that offer 12 core lessons each. I'm also planning to implement automatic downloads of audio files for courses using TTS.


**Structuring the App**

I'm now focusing on defining the app's overall structure and component breakdown. I've decided on the naming conventions and folder organization for this project. Specifically, the component directory will house elements like the header, course cards, and lesson details, as well as the Gemini API services. My goal is to use the Gemini TTS API for the audio download function of each of the 12 lesson categories, or course templates, as part of the overall design.


**Finalizing App Features**

I'm now fully immersed in the core technical aspects. I've defined a clear project structure, including the `metadata.json`, and am mapping out components like `Header.tsx`, `CourseCard.tsx`, and `LessonContent.tsx`. I've outlined a UI/UX design with a professional theme. The main focus is on the `LessonContent.tsx` component, which will handle lesson content display, Gemini API integration for audio generation via TTS, and the automated download function. I am confident in the direction of the core features.


**Defining Application Needs**

I'm now focusing on user requirements and technical plans. I've broken down the application's core functionality, including the "Giniaz College" name, and the specific course categories. Also, I've outlined the technical implementation details. I am designing the user interface, and I have plans for the core logic, state management, and the Gemini API interaction.


**Defining Course Categories**

I'm now focusing on user needs and application features. I've broken down the requirements. The "Giniaz College" app will offer courses in many subjects. The course categories are: Life Skills, Biashara, Usimamizi, and many others, each with 12 lessons. The app will automatically download audio for each lesson generated by the Gemini TTS API.


**Defining Audio Features**

I am now delving into the audio download functionality using the Gemini TTS API. My approach involves converting lesson text to audio, decoding base64 data, and creating downloadable links. I'll automatically trigger downloads for each lesson, and the file name will match the lesson title.


**Outlining App Features**

I'm now fully immersed in the nitty-gritty of the application's structure. I'm building out the `index.html` structure and setting up the basic UI elements using React and Tailwind CSS. The course categories and lesson outlines are starting to take shape. My next task is coding the core logic for the Gemini API.


**Defining App Functionality**

I'm now integrating all the key elements. I've broken down the React app development. The plan involves the setup of the user interface using Tailwind CSS and the development of the logic for the Gemini API calls. My goal is to automatically trigger audio downloads for lessons, following course and lesson structures. The component structure and routing in `App.tsx` are in progress.


**Prioritizing Core Functionality**

I'm now focusing on integrating the features, especially the audio download function, with the UI. The main aim is to build the lesson content display, including TTS generation. I'm building the components for "Giniaz College" and the "Pakua Sauti" button, ensuring automated audio downloads.


**Prioritizing UI and Backend**

I'm now focusing on the interface layout using Tailwind CSS. I'm building out the `index.html`, course and lesson structure and setting the groundwork for connecting the front-end components. I'm also preparing for the Gemini API call integration in `geminiService.ts`. I am preparing to implement the audio download functionality for lessons in the core workflow.

payload.text: Kwasababu hiki ni chuo , hakikisha kila somo ndani ya template,likifunguliwa litakuwa lefu Sana,tunalenga mwanafunzi apate uchuzi wa kina sawa na level ya chuo, kaulimbiu yetu ni chuo chako MAARIFA ya kina .

**Analyzing the Core Request**

I'm now diving into the user's core request, aiming to create a more authentic college course experience within the "Giniaz College" application. The goal is to ensure each subject template feels fully realized when opened. I'm focusing on the implied need for complete and immersive subject content.


**Refining the Content Length**

My current task is refining the lesson length for the "Giniaz College" app. My initial analysis of the user's requirements is complete. I'm focusing on the lesson templates and aiming to increase the content length to truly reflect college-level depth. My plan is to modify the prompt sent to the Gemini API, especially within the `generateLessons` function in `services/geminiService.ts`, increasing the word count request to a target range of 800-1000 words.


**Expanding Content Depth**

I've taken the user's feedback to heart and I'm now crafting the new, extended prompt for Gemini. My focus is on significantly increasing content length for each lesson within the "Giniaz College" app. I'm aiming for 800-1000 words per lesson to provide that college-level depth, and I'm updating `services/geminiService.ts` accordingly. The prompt now emphasizes comprehensive explanations, practical applications, and examples to embody "MAARIFA ya kina." The `lessonsSchema` description will also be updated to reflect this shift towards richer content.


**Implementing Detailed Content**

I'm now implementing the plan for richer content. The new prompt is ready and emphasizes deep, college-level knowledge with a significantly higher word count target (800+ words). I've updated the `generateLessons` function within `services/geminiService.ts` with the new prompt, asking for detailed explanations, examples, and practical applications in Swahili. The `lessonsSchema` description is also adjusted to reflect the longer lesson lengths and the "MAARIFA ya kina" motto.


**Enhancing Lesson Detail**

I'm now revising the lesson structure to be more comprehensive. The prompt has been updated to strongly suggest a word count of at least 800 words, reflecting college-level standards, and requesting detailed explanations, examples, and practical applications in Swahili. The new prompt is very clear about the desired content. The `lessonsSchema` description has been altered to match the changes, clearly showing that these lessons will be quite long and are designed for a college course.

Nimeelewa kikamilifu. Kaulimbiu "Chuo Chako, MAARIFA ya Kina" ni muhimu sana, na ili kuitimiza, lazima tuhakikishe kila somo linatoa elimu ya kina na ya kutosha, kama vile mwanafunzi angeipata chuoni.

Nimefanya mabadiliko muhimu kwenye maelekezo yanayotumwa kwa Gemini API ili itengeneze maudhui marefu zaidi, yenye uchambuzi wa kina, mifano halisi, na maelezo ya kitaaluma. Sasa, kila somo litakuwa na maudhui ya angalau maneno 800, likilenga kutoa maarifa ya kina yanayojenga uelewa wa mwanafunzi hatua kwa hatua, kutoka misingi hadi dhana za juu.

Haya ndiyo mabadiliko niliyofanya:

I will now create new course objects, assigning an `id`, `title`, `description`, and `icon` for each. I'm reusing existing icons where possible, and I'm confident that the icons selected are a good fit for each topic.
